structured_output.summary: This is a clean submission and it passes all 23 items. The spec `e2e/tests/orders/order-notes.spec.ts` uses the suite's own fixture with `ORDERS_SCENARIO` and the `order` actor. It opens the unpaid scenario order through `findOrderId` and adds a note with a new `OrderPage.addNote` method. It then checks the note in the history before and after a page reload, so persistence is actually proven. The new locators sit on `OrderPage` as readonly role-and-name fields that match the real labels in `OrderHistory.tsx`. There are no hard waits, cleanup code or hard-coded ids, and the provided type check output reports no errors.

items.evidence: After page.reload() the spec asserts historyNote(note) is visible (spec lines 78-81). That would fail if the noteAdd mutation never ran; the input clearing is only used as a wait.
actor: "order" (spec line 61), note visible after adding it (line 75), and note visible after reload (line 80). Each criterion has an assertion.
OrderPage had no note locators or actions. The new ones are added to OrderPage itself, and findOrderId and ORDERS_SCENARIO are reused.
No waitForTimeout or sleeps. addNote waits on a web-first toHaveValue("").
Imports test and expect from ../../fixtures/test.ts, is not tagged parallel(), and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.

Role-and-name locators (textbox "Comment", button "Add Comment") match OrderHistory.tsx:101-111. The history note text has no test id in src, so exact getByText is reasonable, and the reason is documented.
Uses the scenario's existing unpaid order. The only change made is the action under test.
The order id is looked up at test time with findOrderId(config, "unpaid"), and no populatedb values are asserted.
Signs in through the stored session for the order actor via test.use. No UI login and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports "exit 0: no errors", and the spec is under e2e/tests/orders/.
The spec uses only OrderPage members: addNote and historyNote.
noteInput and addNoteButton are readonly fields initialised from this.page, and the existing constructor is unchanged.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (spec lines 66, 72).
One test with a test.step for adding the note and one for the reload.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e (spec line 65).
The header block comment (spec lines 56-60) says what is covered and why it runs as the order actor.
All assertions are web-first (toBeVisible, toHaveValue).
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO and the scenario's order key. The note text is the test's own input, not a scenario value.
No cleanup code and no unique or timestamped names.
No custom timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep .ts. The spec takes test and expect only from the fixture, and the page object imports expect from @playwright/test as draftOrderPage.ts and homePage.ts already do.
No any, casts or untyped gql calls.
Both page-object comments explain why: the box clears before the server saves, and there is no test id to scope the note to.
